the neutrino magnetic moment of order 10−10μB and the solar magnetic field in the range of 1−10G are consistent with the data from the Super-Kamiokande and SNO experiments, provided that the missing Be-7 neutrinos are being absorbed via the RSFP transitions.

(i) the RSFP transitions in a magnetic field are not ruled out by the current data, (ii) the bounds on the magnetic moment and the solar magnetic field depend on the neutrino mass hierarchy, (iii) the bounds on magnetic moment and the field are different in the two hierarchies, and (iv) the bounds are tighter in the normal hierarchy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following issues.
the neutrino oscillations and the solar anti-neutrino fluxes in the presence of RSFP transitions in solar magnetic fields.
the study of solar neutrinos and their interaction with magnetic fields.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the bounds on the neutrino magnetic moment are still not very stringent.
RSFP transitions in general are not ruled out as a possible explanation of the solar neutrinos and the solar antineutrinos.
the RSFP transitions in conjunction with the LMA flavor oscillations can not account for the missing berylliun neutrinos and hence can not explain the solar neutrino puzzle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the neutrino magnetic moment is constrained to be less than or equal to (2–3) x 10 ^{-11} μ _{B} for a typical solar field of 0.2 G.
the neutrino magnetic moments are bounded by a factor of 2.5 times the standard value of the dipole moment for the electron neutrino and 1.5 times for the other neutrinos.
, for the RSFP transitions to play a role in the solar neutrino puzzle, a very strong solar magnetic field is required.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the bounds on the neutrino magnetic moment from the RSFP mechanism are comparable with the bounds from the direct measurements of the magnetic moment of neutrino.
the RSFP transitions are still allowed in the Sun, but the product of the neutrino magnetic moment with the magnetic field in the solar core is severely restricted.
the bounds on neutrino magnetic moment are significantly relaxed for the low and intermediate energy solar neutrinos.
